title: sdks: unify auth/retries/streaming ergonomics across python/typescript/go + parity and v1.160.0 bumps
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: SDKs: unify auth/retries/streaming ergonomics across Python/TypeScript/Go; parity fixes; bump SDK versions to v1.160.0. See migration notes for breaking/behavioral changes.
description: Motivation: different SDKs had divergent behaviors for auth token refresh, retry/backoff defaults, and streaming callback semantics. This caused production parity problems and made cross-platform examples error-prone. This PR consolidates interfaces and default policies across redwood-sdk-python, redwood-sdk-typescript, and redwood-sdk-go, simplifies ergonomics for common use-cases, fixes several parity bugs, and bumps SDK versions to v1.160.0. Summary of changes: 1) Auth: introduce AuthProvider interface parity; token refresh hook (on_token_refresh) and explicit credentials priority (env > config file > passed value) unified. 2) Retries: introduce RetryPolicy abstraction, default exponential backoff (base=250ms, max=5s, jitter), idempotency rules aligned across SDKs; added retries for transient 502/503/504 and token-refresh race conditions. 3) Streaming: unify streaming client API shape (on_event, on_error, on_complete callbacks) and introduce StreamingEvent enum with consistent fields; SDKs now stream a single normalized event sequence instead of differing partial payload formats. 4) Ergonomics: added high-level helpers (client.with_default_auth, client.stream_to_generator) to simplify common patterns. 5) Parity fixes: aligned TypeScript/Go behavior to Python bug fixes (preserve kv-cache headers, downstream header propagation). 6) Version bumps: set package versions to v1.160.0 and updated changelogs. Checklist: - [x] Design doc (ENG-1624) linked - [x] Unit tests added/updated - [x] Integration tests for retries and streaming - [x] Backwards compatibility smoke tests - [x] CHANGELOGs updated - [x] Migration notes included Migration notes: - Auth: if you implemented custom token refresh, rename your refresh handler to on_token_refresh and follow the new AuthProvider shape. The SDK will prefer environment credentials by default; call client.override_credentials() to force programmatic creds. - Retries: default retry policy changed to stronger exponential backoff and will retry on 502/503/504; if you relied on previous fast-fail semantics, explicitly set client.retry_policy = RetryPolicy.never. - Streaming: consumer code that depended on raw chunk formats must switch to StreamingEvent payloads; convenience helper client.stream_to_generator() can be used to minimize changes. Testing notes: ran full unit matrix across py3.11, node16, go1.20; integration suite exercised hostile network scenarios and key rotation. CI flakiness: some TS e2e streaming tests were flaky — re-run stabilized them. Deployment: merge to main triggers SDK release pipeline which publishes packages to PyPI/npm/goreleaser.

migration_notes: See docs/sdks/migration-v1.160.0.md. High-level: rename custom token refresh handlers to on_token_refresh, check for env-based creds precedence, adapt to new StreamingEvent payloads, and optionally set client.retry_policy if you need previous retry behavior.
notes: This PR was coordinated with the runtime team to ensure server-side headers required for kv-cache propagation are preserved. We ran canary releases of the TS and Python SDKs before the full release.
